requirements.quote: `packages/core/src/deadlines/`: a rule engine (period types: days, weeks, months; exclusions; the next working day; vacations) with court calendars per forum, built from the notices feed (holiday lists, vacation notifications).
`apps/worker`: an `orders.poll` job for watched matters (delegated lookups or cleared sources) that ingests new daily orders as soon as they are uploaded.
Directions become proposed obligations with the computed due date, the rule applied and the source anchor; the lawyer confirms (D-017 L2).
Tests: a table of real direction phrasings and expected due dates across holidays and vacations.
Due dates are computed correctly for the fixture table, including vacations and the next-working-day rule. [type:unit]
A new order on a watched matter produces proposed obligations within one poll interval, with a page anchor. [type:integration]
Each obligation shows the rule used ("4 weeks from 22 Oct; court closed 19 Nov, so 20 Nov"). [type:unit]
Due dates need court holidays, vacations and Limitation Act rules (for example, the next working day when the court is closed).
requirements.why: Counsel-owned Limitation Act rule tables are tracked separately under the limitation.enabled flag (#84); this change delivers the next-working-day rule only. Vacation ranges are not in the notices data (notice has a single effective_on), so vacations come from a static per-forum table in code; parsing vacation ranges from notice documents is separate work.

deliverables.change: New domain: index.ts, period.ts (days/weeks/months arithmetic), calendar.ts (CourtCalendar: weekly offs, holiday dates from matched holiday notices via the notices tables, per-forum vacation ranges from a static table), compute.ts (computeDueDate with next-working-day rolling, returns {date, rule} where rule is a sentence like '4 weeks from 22 Oct; court closed 19 Nov, so 20 Nov'). Tests include the fixture table of real phrasings across holidays, vacations, month-end clamping and weekends.

Before submitProposals, recompute dueDate of dated 'within' obligation_from_direction drafts through the deadlines engine using the proceeding's forum calendar and order date, and write the rule sentence into payload.basis (<=500 chars); keep the extracted date and basis when the phrase or forum cannot be resolved. Level stays L2; anchors unchanged.

New: for watches whose latest snapshot lists orders with an href not yet captured, fetch each as a delegated lookup (delegatedFor advocate+matter) through the StatusFetcher, create a capture from the bytes (sha256 dedupe per workspace) so extraction.extract-order runs. Reuse pollCaseWatches caps and skip semantics (uncleared/killed source skipped, never a call without delegatedFor). Export from case-watch/index.ts.

New job system.orders.poll (hourly, singleton, no workspace) calling D3 with the fetcher wired through setStatusFetcherFactory; logs ids and counts only. Register in jobs/registry.ts and jobs/index.ts.
Add ordersPoll to the registry list and its type tuple; export from jobs/index.ts.
Expect 'system.orders.poll' in the registered job names.
Add deadlines domain (deps: notices only if it imports the notices index; else reads tables directly) and add deadlines to extraction's allowed imports.
Document the deadlines domain and the new dependency edges in the same shape as the existing rows.
Register the new runtime exports of @causedeck/core (deadlines, orders poll) in SERVICE_TESTS with real cases, or NOT_A_SERVICE with a reason for pure functions.
Real cross-tenant cases for loadCourtCalendar (B's matched notices do not affect A's calendar) and for the orders poll (workspace B's watch never produces captures in A).
Export the deadlines and orders-poll surface the same way sibling domains are exported.
Add the system.orders.poll row (cron, singleton, purpose) to the jobs table.
Add a ./deadlines export map entry if sibling domains each have one.

preserve.what: RELATIVE_RULE and resolveRelative in packages/intelligence/src/extract/relative.ts keep their plain-calendar behaviour (next dates and 'list after' stay unadjusted); intelligence still never imports @causedeck/core.
system.status.poll and pollCaseWatches caps, kill switch, delegatedFor-only fetching (packages/core/src/case-watch/poll.ts, lookup.ts) are unchanged.
obligation_from_direction stays an always-L2 proposal (packages/core/src/automation/matrix.ts:54); nothing is applied without the lawyer's confirmation.

pnpm --filter @causedeck/worker exec vitest run src/__tests__/registry.test.ts src/__tests__/schedules.test.ts --maxWorkers=${FORGE_HOST_PARALLELISM:-1} --reporter=dot
pnpm --filter @causedeck/intelligence exec vitest run src/extract/relative.test.ts src/extract/to-proposals.test.ts --maxWorkers=${FORGE_HOST_PARALLELISM:-1} --reporter=dot

decisions.choice: Adjustment lives in core (extraction/run.ts), not in packages/intelligence.
decisions.justification: intelligence imports nothing from core (packages/intelligence/src/extract/index.ts:1-3) and the calendar needs DB reads of matched notices (packages/core/src/notices/holidays.ts).

decisions.choice: No migration: vacation ranges come from a static per-forum table in code, holidays from existing notice.effective_on.
decisions.justification: notice has a single effective_on date and no range column (packages/db/src/schema/notices.ts:61); schema work would need counsel-sourced data and a migration number outside this scope.

decisions.choice: orders.poll reuses the delegated StatusFetcher and pollCaseWatches caps instead of a new fetch path.
decisions.justification: All external reads must go through the governed fetch layer with delegatedFor (packages/core/src/case-watch/lookup.ts:1-8, poll.ts:1-8).
